subject: High resolution and small area data

messages.author: fea49925f53af1fc
messages.subject: High resolution and small area data
parts:
Hi Chris and everybody,
Hope everything is well with you!

I was wondering if your framework would work well with my data and also wanted to ask what is the best way to proceed with it.

Basically I have GPS fairly high resolution data every 5 seconds. This data was extracted from fitness bands I put in some fishers in my study area. The thing is that a good amount of the data has >5 lag between observations. I know the 10, 20 or 30s are not a big problem, but I think when the fishers spent two much time static, the band (probably to save energy) stopped recording the GPS. Also there are a few GPS pure location errors, which I guess would not be a big problem since your framework accounts for that.

1 - Do you think it is ok to use your framework in a small area (5000m2)?
2 - What would you recommend me to do in the sense that I am not interested in getting their home range, I just want to have a clean track data (LAT/LONG) which I will model afterwards.

My data structure has this columns: TIME | ID | LAT | LONG

I thank you in advance,
Cheers
João

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: High resolution and small area data
parts:
Hi João,

The 5 seconds isn't an issue if you can model the location error, but the fix rate being a function of the acceleration is an issue in any model that doesn't account for that (which is everything published). If you only collect data when accelerating, then models not knowing that will assume similar behavior when the data are not being collected.

If you run something like ctmm::predict() with an error model, then it will interpolate between the gaps evenly (because it doesn't know about the acceleration-informed sampling), when maybe you want more weight on the last location fix before the gap. You could potentially use that to estimate the last fix before the gap better and then fill the gap with that, up to some lag, and then re-run predict().

Whether or not 1/2 a hectare is too small depends on how large the location errors are, and what you are trying to get out of the data, and whether or not your analyses can include the error model.

Best,
Chris
